tested_change: packages/agent_runtime/runtime_service.py: AgentRunService.open_stream uses the prepared run version for both the event emitter and graph initial state.
environment: Separate synthetic workspaces for before and after. Real FastAPI, PostgreSQL and checkpoint persistence; loopback deterministic model and synthetic ticket only. No paid provider calls.

stream_recovery.fault: The worker-mode API prepared a run, then its injected queue raised ConnectionError on enqueue. HTTP returned 503 RUN_DISPATCH_UNAVAILABLE before the model started. Another API on the same database accepted the identical turn token after publication.

durable_reconnect.observation: GET replay returns persisted events after the cursor. Transient token deltas are not part of the durable log.

stream_recovery.before_reconnect: Not measured; the before observation covers the live retry.

http_observations.derive: Deriving v1 returned its prompt while the draft still held v2. Explicit PATCH applied the returned draft-owned values. Preflight kept the independently cleared tool bindings. The original v1 snapshot and completed run read back unchanged.

knowledge_and_tool_binding.coverage: Separate PostgreSQL integration cases; the HTTP ticket fixture has no knowledge base.
knowledge_and_tool_binding.pinned: The pinned snapshot remains fixed after source revisions retire. A published version retains its tool revision after another revision is published.
knowledge_and_tool_binding.latest: The published LATEST selector resolves the effective snapshot for a new run; observe the persisted snapshot for an existing run or recovery. The selector itself does not change older version records.

reproduce: Use a fresh workspace, an owner, a viewer, two local deterministic model profiles with distinguishable outputs, and a synthetic customer. Run two API instances on the same test database: inline execution and worker execution with an enqueue stub that raises before dispatch.

POST /agents; bind create_ticket using PUT /agents/{a}/tool-bindings; POST /agents/{a}/publish for v1. POST /agents/{a}/threads. Submit a normal turn and another requiring ticket approval via POST /threads/{t}/turns. Keep their tokens, versions and run IDs.

POST /threads/{t}/turns/stream using the failing worker API. After the 503, change the draft prompt/profile and remove the tool, then publish v2. Retry the exact text and token on the inline API. Compare every live frame version with GET /agent-runs/{run}; reconnect via GET /agent-runs/{run}/stream?after_sequence=1.

Retry the completed turn, change its body with the same token, submit a fresh token and a turn on a new thread. Send a direct POST /agent-versions/{v1}/runs. Approve the original pending action twice via POST /approvals/{id}/approve and count the customer tickets.

Use POST /agents/{a}/versions/{v1}/derive, inspect the unchanged draft, explicitly PATCH the returned values and preflight. Publish the unchanged draft concurrently twice. Repeat protected calls as viewer and read the version using another workspace.
limits: The injected failure covers rejection before queue dispatch. A real broker, dispatch acknowledgement loss after delivery, and process-wide crash recovery were not exercised by the HTTP fixture.
Approval executed one local synthetic ticket. Browser cache behavior, paid-model behavior, and external side effects were outside this verification.
